identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log — Toyota 8FGU25, Unit FL-2 (Portland Warehouse), September 2026

scan.summary: This is a daily pre-shift inspection log for a single propane-powered forklift (Toyota 8FGU25, unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse, kept to satisfy the shift-inspection requirement in 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). It records tick/defect status across a dozen safety checklist items for each shift the truck was used and lists the two certified operators and their next evaluation due dates. As a record, it is judged on whether the entries are complete and current, not against a written standard.
scan.freshness_note: Last entry is dated September 18, 2026. Today is September 27, 2026 — nine calendar days, including at least six weekdays, have no inspection entries, so the log does not cover the most recent operating period.

gaps.title: Missing entries between Sep 2 and Sep 7
gaps.description: No inspection rows exist for Sep 3–6, yet the hour meter shows the truck accumulated hours in that span, meaning it was operated without a documented pre-shift inspection on those days.
gaps.fix: Backfill or explain the gap with a supervisor note, and reinforce with operators that every shift of use — not just weekdays — requires a logged inspection per 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7).
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Log ends before the current date
gaps.description: The log's last entry is Sep 18, but today is Sep 27 — nine days, including several weekdays, are not represented, so there is no record of pre-shift inspections (or lack of them) for the most recent period.
gaps.fix: Continue the log through the full month and produce it promptly when requested; confirm whether inspections occurred Sep 19–27 and record them.

gaps.title: Horn defect closed out without a documented corrective action
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn was marked defective with the note 'Horn not working,' and the checklist instructs that a truck with a safety-affecting defect not be used, but there is no entry showing the truck was tagged out of service, who repaired it, or when — the next day's row simply shows the horn passing again.
gaps.fix: Add a corrective-action note (date, technician/parts, and out-of-service status) whenever a defect is logged, so the record shows the truck was not used until the safety defect was corrected.

gaps.title: Supervisor review not completed
gaps.description: The log has a supervisor review signature and date line, but both are blank for the month shown, so there is no evidence a supervisor checked the entries or the defect handling.
gaps.fix: Have a supervisor sign and date the monthly review line before filing the log.

scan.confidence_notes: I'm confident in what is on the page — the checklist, the dates, the defect note, and the operator evaluation dates are all read directly from the log. I'm reasonably confident that 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) is the correct governing citation and that Oregon OSHA enforces it under the same federal numbering, based on Oregon OSHA's own rule text referencing '§1910.178, Powered Industrial Trucks, in Subdivision N.' I'm less certain about the site being 'company-wide' versus Portland-only, since only one site is listed for this company, and about whether the missing days after Sep 18 reflect non-operation (e.g., truck idle) versus un-logged use — the document does not say.
